subject: Post-call: tool/function calling patterns + integration approach for Finarc POC

Subject: Post-call recap: tool/function calling patterns + integration approach for Finarc POC

Hi Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we can get the POC moving this week. I captured the parts we discussed plus a recommended simplest-viable architecture for the first sprint.

High-level asks we heard:
- POC goal: 90th percentile < 350ms tail latency for user search flows; improved precision on top-3 results via embeddings+reranker; store audit logs for 30 days.
- Security: VPC-private control plane, KMS-managed keys, SSO for admin UI, API keys for app-to-service.
- Integration scope: search augmentation (embedding lookup), structured tool calls (payment lookup, account actions), and a reranker service to lift top-k.

Recommended architecture (Sprint 0):
1) SDK + auth: give you the SDK quickstart (node/python) + service account flow for server-side calls. For browser flows use short-lived token exchange (backend mints ephemeral tokens).
2) Tool definitions: canonicalize 3 tool types in the manifest — search_query (embedding vector lookup), account_mutation (DB write via internal API), external_lookup (third-party data fetch). Each tool schema should include name, input_schema (JSON Schema), timeout_ms, retry_policy.
3) Parallel/async pattern: run search_query + external_lookup in parallel (soft timeout 300ms), then call reranker serially on combined candidates. If both parallel calls fail, return cached top-3 and surface a graceful error to the client.
4) Structured output: enforce a small JSON schema for model outputs (choices[].tool_call.name, choices[].tool_call.args) so your frontend can wire UI actions without NLP parsing. We’ll provide a sample JSON Schema.
5) Embeddings/rerank: initial approach — FAISS on 1536-d embeddings (open-source model), budget later to evaluate approximate vs exact depending on recall. Reranker should be an encoder-cross-attention model called only on top-20 candidates to control cost.

Tradeoffs we flagged on the call:
- Parallel external_lookup increases tail-risk; mitigate with 300ms cutoff and circuit-breaker to avoid cascading timeouts.
- Rerankers improve precision but cost more per query — recommend run-rate sampling for measuring ROI before full rollout.

Action items / next steps:
- I’ll share the integration checklist and a draft manifest (attached).
- Rishi will send a short sample routing + tool manifest snippet (auth headers, timeout, fallback).
- Priya: confirm whether DevOps prefers SSO or API key for the initial POC and whether we can get a sandbox DB credential by Wed.
- We’ll schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive next Tue for the DevOps + engineering team.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (pdf), poC-scope-sheet.xlsx (xls)

Thanks —
Aisha
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Priya — quick technical answers and a sample config to help your SAML/devops folks scope work.

1) Control plane / VPC: Redwood supports two options: (a) Managed VPC — we create a dedicated VPC in our account and peer via VPC peering/VPN; (b) Customer-hosted control plane (private deployment) — we deliver a deployable bundle to run the control plane in your AWS account (requires minimal infra: 2 subnets, an EKS or ECS cluster, and access to your KMS). For the POC, customer-hosted is recommended if you need KMS-integration without sending keys out.

2) KMS: we can integrate with your AWS KMS customer-managed keys (CMK) when you run the private control plane. For hosted trials we usually offer Redwood-managed KMS for speed; we will not have access to your plaintext keys in either mode.

3) SDK auth flow: yes — the SDK quickstart contains two patterns. Example (pseudo):

// server-side (mint ephemeral)
POST /auth/mint-token
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <service-account-secret>
Response: { "ephemeral_token": "ey..", "expires_in": 900 }

// browser call
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_token>

4) Failure UX: recommended pattern from ops: if both parallel calls fail, return cached results + boolean meta {source: "cache", degraded: true} and surface a small banner in the UI: "Results are temporarily degraded; try again in a few seconds." This keeps the user flow intact.

Sample tool manifest snippet (JSON-like in email):

{ "tools": [
  {"name": "search_query", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"q":{"type":"string"}}}, "timeout_ms": 300, "retry_policy": "none"},
  {"name": "external_lookup", "input_schema": {"type":"object", "properties": {"id":{"type":"string"}}}, "timeout_ms": 300, "retry_policy": "short_backoff"},
  {"name": "account_mutation", "input_schema": {"type":"object", "properties": {"account_id":{"type":"string"},"op":{"type":"string"}}}, "timeout_ms": 500, "retry_policy": "idempotent_retry"}
]}

Notes: enable KV prefix caching for repeated prefixes (search query embeddings) to lower ops cost; batch embedding lookups (vector size 1536) with a 128-vector batch window where possible. For reranking, use a top-20 candidate threshold to keep cross-attention cost bounded.

SDK versions we recommend for POC: redwood-sdk-js@0.9.x and redwood-sdk-py@0.9.x (they include function-calling helpers + manifest validation).

Happy to paste a runnable example in the tech deep-dive.

—Rishi
